- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot upward momentum.
- Underestimate downward corrections after negative sentiment; model fails to react to bearish sentiment signals.
- Lag in price response to sentiment shifts: model reacts slowly to sentiment turning points, especially negative sentiment.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to smoothly revert to historical mean when sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish.
- Overshoots in early forecast periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; correct by reducing initial slope.
- When sentiment is consistently positive, model overestimates upside; when sentiment is consistently negative, model underestimates downside.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; model should not extrapolate too aggressively from short-term trends without sentiment confirmation.
- Adjust forecast downward if sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes or prolonged bearish sentiment.
- Increase downward bias if sentiment history includes multiple negative sentiment days with no reversal signal.
